label: diffuse token-identity unit (input b/p/2/x/m; outputs e/v/h/x)
explanation: Active on about 1% of steps, split evenly between the original phase and the copy phase. It almost never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, or on the first two copy outputs. The rate rises toward the end of long sequences (L=9, late orig_idx). The firing is spread across many token identities and gives only weak lifts (4-5x): input b/p/2/x/m (and o/v/w), previous input q/p/b, and copy-phase outputs e/v/h/x. A disjunction of copy-phase output in {e,v,h,x} OR original-phase input in {b,p,2,x,m} captures about 73% of the activation mass on dev, but its precision is about 5%. Conjunctions with prev_tok raise precision only to about 11-13% (F1 about 0.16). No coherent predicate explains when it fires. It seems to read a distributed token or hidden-state code rather than a single interpretable condition. I did not check magnitude modulation beyond the length/position trend.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & in_tok=p (+7.02), t=1 & in_tok=b (+6.98), t=1 & in_tok=2 (+6.92), t=1 & prev_tok=b (+6.61), t=1 & prev_tok=2 (+6.60), t=1 & prev_tok=q (+6.59). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-8.10), in_tok=h (-4.22), in_tok=f (-4.03), in_tok=u (-3.51).
